meta.title: Finnish A1 Beginner
meta.subtitle: 500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Finnish → English (see the Finnish, recall the meaning) and English → Finnish (see an English meaning, recall the Finnish). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 500 words of Finnish for a beginner, aligned to A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases aimed at the satisfaction of needs of a concrete type' — a learner here is able to introduce themselves and others, to ask and answer questions about personal details such as where they live, people they know and things they have, and to interact in a simple way provided the other person talks slowly and clearly and is prepared to help. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Finnish has an examination graded to these levels (the National Certificates of Language Proficiency, YKI), but no graded word list for it was found published, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 345 of the 500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — greetings and politeness, introducing yourself, family, numbers, telling the time, days and months, food and drink, shopping and money, the home, the town and getting about, the body and feeling ill, the weather and the seasons, colours, and the pronouns, question words, postpositions and particles every sentence is built out of — and the other 155 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Finnish, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case of a noun and every form of a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Verbs are given as Finnish dictionaries give them, in the first infinitive (syödä "to eat", puhua "to speak"). The 185 nouns show their plural, their genitive, their partitive and their plural partitive, the forms consonant gradation and stem changes make hard to guess (käsi, kädet, käden, kättä, käsiä), and behind the All forms fold every case in both numbers; the 103 verbs show their "I" and "he, she" forms, their past and their perfect (syödä: syön, syö, söi, on syönyt), and behind the fold the present, the negative, the past, the perfect, the conditional and the imperative by person, and the passive. The Finnish Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters and their sounds. Real example sentences come with 500 of the 500 words, three apiece for 498 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
